items.title: Is Carvana (CVNA) a Buy as Wall Street Analysts Look Optimistic?
items.summary: Based on the average brokerage recommendation (ABR), Carvana (CVNA) should be added to one's portfolio. Wall Street analysts' overly optimistic recommendations cast doubt on the effectiveness of this highly sought-after metric. So, is the stock worth buying?

items.title: CVNA Q3 deep dive: operational efficiency and platform expansion drive growth amid margin pressures
items.summary: Online used car dealer Carvana (NYSE: CVNA) reported Q3 2026 results beating Wall Street’s revenue expectations, with sales up 42.4% year on year to $8.04 billion. Its non-GAAP profit of $0.39 per share was 18.3% below analysts’ consensus estimates.

items.title: Carvana (CVNA) Stock Fair Value Edges Lower After Analysts Trim Growth Assumptions
items.summary: The latest Carvana model update edges the central fair value estimate lower, from US$82.98 to US$80.86 per share. That modest adjustment fits with a tight cluster of analyst targets between roughly US$72 and US$90, reflecting investors weighing upbeat views on Q3 execution against concerns around interest rates, margins, and the auto retail backdrop.
